messages:
kevin: Quick check — small RFC follow-up idea: split the current Resolver into two pieces: DecisionSkeleton and OutcomeScorer. Want quick feedback on the interface shape before I open a PR.

alice: Can you sketch what each piece would own?

kevin: Sure. Rough responsibilities: DecisionSkeleton = gather signals (region, tenant prefs, recent affinity), apply deterministic tie-breakers, return a candidate set + lightweight hints. OutcomeScorer = expensive scoring (latency/cost/model-pref), can be hot-reloaded or run async, returns final ranking + per-candidate scores/metadata.

maria: Sounds reasonable. Main concern: latency path. We can't add copies or allocs on hot path. How do you pass candidates without heavy copying?

kevin: Plan is immutable CandidateRef objects (id + pointer to shared metadata) — no deep copy. DecisionSkeleton returns CandidateRefs and maybe a tiny `score_hint` float. Example payload: ```{"candidates":[{"id":"gpu-pool-3","score_hint":0.12},{"id":"cpu-cache-1","score_hint":-0.03}]}```

sam: How do we handle scorer failure/timeouts? Today resolver must return something synchronously.

kevin: We'll require DecisionSkeleton to include a baked fallback ordering (based on static heuristics + hint). Runtime policy: if Scorer times out or fails, use fallback ordering. Also attach a metric `policy.scorer.timeout` and increment circuit-breaker.

jess: Compatibility with adapters: they expect route IDs and a stable API. Migration path?

kevin: Two-step migration: (1) Sidecar mode where DecisionSkeleton delegates to old resolver; (2) rollout OutcomeScorer behind feature-flag; provide an adapter shim that maps CandidateRef -> route id for legacy adapters. Deprecate old path after canary.

deploy-bot: :rocket: canary plan created: canary=5% traffic, regions=[eu-west-1], duration=48h.

maria: Telemetry additions: span tags for decision.hash, scorer.version, fallback_used (bool), plus counters for tie-breaker hits. Also include per-candidate reason_code for auditability.

sam: Tie-breaker determinism across replicas is important. We should avoid per-replica randomness causing flapping. Suggest consistent hashing over tenant_id + request_id, plus an opt-in sticky seed per cluster.

alice: Also prefer last-seen affinity if available so warmed shards get picked. That reduces cold-starts. Make it an explicit weighted factor in DecisionSkeleton.

kevin: Agreed. Implementation notes I'll put in RFC: - CandidateRef = {id, score_hint(float32, -1..1), affinity_score(float32)} - DecisionSkeleton returns ordered CandidateRef[] + tie_break_seed - OutcomeScorer takes CandidateRef[] and returns scored list + reason codes - Timeout semantics: scorer_timeout_ms (configurable) -> fallback_to_skeleton ordering.

jess: Please ensure reason codes map to human-readable strings (for audit/logging) and an enum for programmatic checks.

maria: One more ops note: expose `policy.decision.latency` histogram and a boolean `fallback_used` tag to alert when scorer regresses.

kevin: Thanks — I'll draft RFC with a proto sketch and tests: deterministic tie-breaker test, scorer-timeout test, adapter-shim test. Plan to open PR by EOD and ping reviewers.

alice: :thumbsup: Prefer small PRs: interface + unit tests, then separate refactor.

sam: Lgtm. Ping infra for canary config when PR is up.

kevin: Will do — thanks everyone.
